topic: Ballot–Kimberling–Moses (2017), Section 5, Table 5, page 23: the x^2-2x+1 recurrence
title: Resolving the double-root conjecture in Ballot–Kimberling–Moses (2017), Section 5, Table 5, p. 23

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We prove the conjectured recurrence for q(x)=x^2-2x+1 in Ballot–Kimberling–Moses (2017), Section 5, Table 5, page 23. The polynomial-form tree has G_n=1+binomial(n,2) for every n>=0, so its recurrence with coefficients (3,-3,1) holds from n=3. Value-and-derivative coordinates give an exact shortest-path formula. We also prove G_n=n for n>=1 modulo x^2-1, correcting G_3 from 4 to 3, and G_n=6n-20 for n>=6 modulo x^2-x+1, with recurrence starting at n=8. For x^m-1 we give exact distances and the count sum of binomial(n-1,r) for 0<=r<m and n>=1.
summary: Written proofs give exact distances and counts for the double-root, simple cyclic and hexagonal quotients, their generating functions, and a cyclic-quotient family. The pinned Lean declaration result proves the double-root recurrence with N=3. Exact finite checks cover the three quadratic quotients through depth 80 and x^m-1 for 1<=m<=6 through depth 16. The coverage table accounts for all source table rows and numbered conjectures, with prior results credited separately.
